feedback_text: The 200+ filter screener is genuinely one of the best in the Indian market. I can build custom screens around ROCE > 20%, debt-to-equity < 0.5, and promoter holding > 50% with ease. It saves me hours every weekend.

The financial data for most large-caps is accurate and timely. But for small-cap and micro-cap stocks, I've noticed balance sheet numbers that don't match BSE filings. Had one case where FY23 revenue was wrong by 20%. This needs fixing urgently.

Basic financial ratios like 10-year ROE history are locked behind Pro. For a research tool targeting serious investors, this feels too aggressive. Even Screener.in gives more historical data on the free tier.
The pre-built screens like 'Consistent Compounders' and 'High ROCE Low Debt' are excellent starting points. I tweak them with my own filters and it becomes a powerful discovery engine.
Quarterly results sometimes take 2-3 days to reflect after the company announces on exchanges. During earnings season, this is frustrating. A competitor updates within hours. Please fix this lag.
I love that I can export screener results to Excel. The Pro export is clean and well-structured. Wish the free plan allowed at least limited exports.
Peer comparison tables are very useful for sector-level analysis. I compare 8-10 companies in the same industry at once. Data is generally accurate for NSE-listed entities.
The paywall pops up even when I'm browsing a basic stock page. Trying to view a simple 5-year EPS trend and it asks me to subscribe. This is annoying for casual research.

Custom screener formulas with nested conditions are a game changer. I built a screen combining Altman Z-score proxies and it's been incredibly useful. Best screener for fundamental investors in India.
The promoter pledging data shows a delay. I found a stock where pledging had gone to 60% but Tickertape still showed the old number. This is critical data and it needs to be real-time.

The stock page layout is clean and logically structured — from overview to financials to shareholding. It flows naturally for a research workflow. Minor complaint: font size on mobile could be larger for number-heavy tables.
Free screener is decent for basic filtering but you hit paywalls very quickly. I understand it's a business, but 3 saves should be allowed on the free plan instead of zero.
The screener history and saved screens persist across devices, which is very convenient. I start a research session on desktop and continue on mobile without losing my filters.

Found that for one mid-cap company the net profit margin was showing incorrect values for two consecutive quarters. Filed a report through the app but got no response. Data errors on a paid plan are unacceptable.

The ability to screen by management quality proxies — like consistent dividend payout, no share dilution, low capital WIP — is something I haven't found anywhere else in India. Tickertape Pro is worth the subscription for this alone.
Good interface overall but the mobile app screener is not as powerful as the web. On mobile, I can't see all active filters at a glance. Need a filter summary panel on the screener mobile view.
The historical financial data goes back 10+ years for most large caps, which is great for long-term trend analysis. Only issue is that the data for a few SME IPO companies is missing or incomplete.

The screener is powerful but filters can't be drag-and-drop reordered. Once I've set 12 filters, going back to change priority requires deleting and re-adding. This is a basic UX issue that should have been fixed long ago.
The Market Mood Index is a genuinely useful sentiment gauge. I use it as a contrarian signal — when it hits Extreme Greed I get cautious. Nice that it shows historical MMI overlaid with Nifty.

The 14-day trial requiring credit card authorization felt like a dark pattern. I entered my card details and was charged on day 15 with zero reminder. Had to dispute with my bank. Please send a reminder before charging.

Ability to combine technical and fundamental filters in the same screen is underrated. I can find stocks with good fundamentals AND currently in an RSI oversold zone. This cross-filter capability is excellent.
Price alerts work fine, but I want alerts triggered by fundamental events — like when quarterly PAT growth drops below 10%, or when debt-to-equity crosses a threshold. That would be a power feature.

I've been using Screener.in and Trendlyne for years. Tickertape Pro now genuinely competes, especially for visual presentation and mobile experience. The screener is the strongest part of the product.
Cash flow statement data is sometimes inconsistent — operating cash flow totals don't always reconcile with line items. Minor accounting display bug but it confuses me when I'm building DCF models.

The analyst consensus data — buy/hold/sell ratios and price targets — is a useful addition, especially for cross-checking my own thesis. Tickertape seems to aggregate multiple analyst views which adds reliability.
Wrote to support about a data discrepancy in FII holding percentages. Got an auto-reply and then silence for 10 days. For a paid subscriber, the support response time is simply not acceptable.
The stock discovery page is a bit cluttered with too many feature cards. I want a clean, fast way to reach the stock financials page without scrolling through marketing content.
Corporate actions data — rights issues, bonus, splits, buybacks — is well-maintained and reflects accurately in the charts. This is critical for long-term performance tracking.

For fundamental investors, the charts are adequate. But there are no annotations, no ability to mark key events on price charts. If I could mark earnings dates or news events on the chart, that would be very helpful.
Shareholding pattern history with quarter-on-quarter FII/DII change is excellent. I can quickly spot when smart money is quietly exiting a stock.

I just started investing last year and Tickertape has been my go-to app. The interface is clean and doesn't overwhelm me. The Investment Scorecard gives me a quick sense of whether a stock is good without needing to read financial statements.

Every time I try to dig deeper into a stock I hit a paywall. I understand the premium model, but even basic things like 5-year EPS growth or debt history should be visible to free users. Other apps give more for free.
The onboarding was really smooth. Setting up my watchlist and linking my Groww account took less than 5 minutes. I could see all my holdings on Tickertape right away. Very beginner-friendly.

The app is visually nice but some financial terms are not explained. When I see ROCE or EV/EBITDA I don't know what it means. Screener.in has tooltips that explain each metric. Tickertape should add this too.
The Market Mood Index is my favorite feature. Before I invest, I check if the market is in Fear or Greed territory. It's such a simple but powerful concept presented beautifully. Love it.

Downloaded the app to learn about stocks. Within 10 minutes, I was hit with upsell banners everywhere. I felt like I was on a sales website, not a learning tool. Would have preferred a less pushy experience.
The curated portfolios from SEBI-registered advisors are very helpful for beginners like me. I used them as templates to build my first portfolio. Clear rationale for each stock picks.
The app is good but the home screen feels like there's too much happening. As a new investor, I don't need 10 different cards. A simplified beginner mode would help a lot.
I had a question about how portfolio analysis works and tried to reach support. No chat support, only email. Waited 4 days for a reply. For a beginner needing quick answers, this is very frustrating.
The pre-built screens are perfect for beginners. 'Consistent Compounders', 'Dividend Aristocrats', 'High Growth Stocks' — these gave me great ideas when I didn't know where to start.

I signed up for the 14-day free trial and got charged on day 15 with no prior notification. I didn't realize I had authorized recurring payment. The app should send a reminder 2-3 days before the trial ends.
Love how stock news is curated on the stock page itself. I can read relevant news without jumping to Google. Makes research much more self-contained for a beginner.
Upgraded to Pro thinking I'd understand the screener better. But the screener still feels complex. Need more beginner-friendly templates and maybe a guided 'build your first screen' tutorial flow.
The explanation of MMI categories — Extreme Fear to Extreme Greed — is very educational. I learned what these mean just by reading the descriptions in the app. Great approach to financial literacy.
The stock comparison feature is useful but limited to 3 stocks. When I'm comparing sector peers I often need to compare 5-6 companies at once. Please allow at least 5.
Best-looking investment research app in India. The charts, color coding, and cards are beautifully designed. Even my non-investing friends find it easy to use.

I was researching a stock and the description on the company page was completely outdated — it said the company operated in a segment it had divested 2 years ago. Basic company profile data needs regular auditing.

The portfolio health check flagging red flags in my holdings is excellent. It highlighted that I was overexposed to one sector and had overlapping stocks. Very valuable for a beginner building their first portfolio.
Price alerts are useful but I want an alert type that says 'this stock entered your custom screener criteria.' That would be incredibly useful for passive investors who don't check the app every day.
Tried to link my Angel One account. The sync kept failing. Unlinked and re-linked three times. Finally gave up. If the core portfolio sync doesn't work, the whole app feels useless.
The SIP calculator on mutual fund pages is simple and effective. I could quickly see what a ₹5,000 monthly SIP would grow to over 15 years. Helped me visualize my retirement goal.
Would love a learning section inside the app — short videos or articles explaining financial ratios and how to use the screener. Right now I have to go to YouTube to understand what I'm looking at.

The Investment Checklist on each stock — scoring profitability, valuation, entry point, and growth — is brilliant for someone like me who is still learning. It gives me a structured way to evaluate a stock.
The app crashes every time I try to open a mutual fund page on my Samsung A32. Checked and the app is updated. This happens consistently. Please fix the stability issue on mid-range Android devices.

Tickertape was the first investing app that didn't feel intimidating to me. The clean design, simple language, and well-organized information made me feel like I could actually understand the stock market.
The free tier is good for browsing but you can't save watchlists beyond a limit without Pro. I'd be okay paying a small fee if the limit was higher, but the current free cap is too restrictive.
The 'Bulk Deals' section is something I'd never seen explained clearly before. Tickertape makes it easy to see who is buying large quantities and when. Very educational feature.
Search on the app is inconsistent. Searching for a company by its short name or brand name often returns nothing. I have to type the exact registered company name to find it. This needs improvement.
The color-coded score cards for stocks make it very easy to quickly gauge quality. Green/yellow/red at a glance is intuitive for someone who doesn't want to read 50 metrics.
The diversification score is interesting but I don't always understand how it's calculated. A breakdown showing what's pulling the score down would make this feature much more actionable.

Tickertape is not for active traders. The charts are way too basic compared to TradingView. No multi-timeframe analysis, no ability to draw trend lines or Fibonacci levels. I use it only for fundamental screening.
On the free plan, stock prices are delayed by 15 minutes. For a swing trader trying to time entries and exits, this is essentially useless. Even with Pro, I'm not sure the data is truly real-time.

The RSI and SMA indicators in the screener are useful for scanning. But the chart itself doesn't support adding custom indicators. I want MACD, Bollinger Bands, Volume Profile — none of these are available.

For swing traders, the RSI < 30 screen is a good entry point discovery tool. I use it to generate a watchlist of oversold stocks and then use TradingView for detailed chart analysis. Good for pre-screening.
The chart interface lags during market hours. Price candles take 3-5 seconds to update. For intraday or swing trading, this lag is unacceptable. TradingView handles real-time charts much better.

The combination of technical screener filters with fundamentals is where Tickertape shines for traders. I can find stocks that are technically oversold but have strong balance sheets — that's a unique edge.
MMI is a useful macro sentiment tool. I use it to decide whether to be aggressive or defensive in my swing trades. Works as a good 30,000-foot sentiment check.

As an active trader, Tickertape's charting module is a major disappointment. No drawing tools, no alert on technical indicator conditions, no option chain data. This is analysis software, not trading software.

Price alerts are useful but too simplistic. I want alerts when a stock crosses a moving average, or when volume spikes above average. These are basic features that any trading-focused app should have.
The ability to screen stocks using EMA crossovers is a genuinely useful trading filter. Not many platforms offer this in a screener format. Tickertape gets credit for thinking about trader use cases.

Looked up a stock during the trading session and the volume data on Tickertape was showing yesterday's figure. This is embarrassing for a market data app. Data freshness needs to be addressed urgently.

Switching between stocks in the screener results is slow. There's too much page reload every time I click a stock. I want a slide-in panel or split-screen view to compare multiple screener results without losing context.
The 52-week high/low screens and momentum screens are good for identifying breakout candidates. I use these as input for my weekly watchlist alongside TradingView charts.
Tried to use Tickertape for intraday analysis. The charts don't even support 5-minute candles. Minimum is daily. This is not suitable for any kind of active trading. Clear gap in the product.
Delivery percentage data is not reliably updated. For swing trading, delivery % is a critical signal and it often shows blank or stale data. This gap makes me rely on NSE website directly.

FII/DII activity data in the screener is very useful. I built a screen that flags stocks with increasing FII holding over 3 consecutive quarters — excellent for identifying institutional accumulation.
The one-click buy from screener results via Zerodha integration is useful but the execution flow is clunky. Takes too many taps. Should be max 2 taps from screener to order confirmation.

The app slows down significantly between 9:15 AM and 11 AM, exactly when I need it most. Loading a stock page can take 8-10 seconds during market open. This is a real problem for time-sensitive decisions.

Tickertape is a research tool, not a trading terminal. Once I understood that, I started using it appropriately. For quick fundamental checks before entering a trade, it's good. But chart-based trading — use TradingView.
The bulk deals screener is gold for traders. I track institutional block deals to see where smart money is moving. The filters and historic data are well-maintained for this feature.

Alert notifications are delayed. I set an alert for a price level and got the notification 12 minutes after the stock had already crossed it. An alert that arrives late is useless for any active trading context.
Would love if MMI had sector-level sentiment indices — not just the overall market. Knowing that IT sector sentiment is in fear while FMCG is in greed would be very actionable.
The volume anomaly screener — stocks with unusual volume spikes — is a great addition. Volume is often the first signal of institutional activity and having this built into a screener is very useful.
Options chain data is missing entirely. As someone who trades options alongside equities, I'd love to see options OI, PCR, and max pain data on Tickertape. That would make it a one-stop shop.
The watchlist widget for the home screen is very handy. I can glance at my tracked stocks without opening the full app. Response time could be faster but the design is clean and functional.
For a platform called Ticker-Tape, the charts are ironically the weakest part. No intraday, no drawing tools, no custom indicators. The name suggests real-time data but the reality is far from it.

The mutual fund screener is the best I've used in India. I can filter by Sharpe ratio, alpha, expense ratio, fund manager tenure, AUM all at once. It took me 10 minutes to build my 3-fund portfolio from scratch.
The MF screener doesn't have a 'Modified Duration' filter for debt funds. For someone investing in duration funds, this is a critical gap. Screener.in has it, Tickertape doesn't. Please add it.
Tracking all my SIPs across Zerodha Coin, Groww, and MFCentral in one view is extremely convenient. The unified portfolio view with XIRR calculation across all SIPs is very helpful.
The MF screener is good but fund overlap analysis is behind a paywall. Understanding how much my three equity funds overlap in holdings is a fundamental research need, not a premium luxury.

Finally an app that shows rolling returns instead of just trailing returns for mutual funds. Point-to-point returns are misleading and Tickertape's rolling return charts give a much more honest picture.
The NAV data is updated daily, which is fine for mutual funds. But when I'm trying to calculate my actual XIRR, the transaction import from CAMS is sometimes incomplete or missing a few months.
The fund manager history and AMC profile section is very underrated. I check how a fund manager has performed across different tenures and market cycles before investing. Great research depth.

The SIP calculator is good but lacks a step-up SIP option. Most systematic investors increase their SIP by 10% each year and the absence of this simple feature in the calculator feels like an oversight.
The portfolio overlap checker is excellent. Found that my large-cap and flexi-cap funds had 65% overlap. Immediately adjusted my allocation. This feature alone justifies the Pro subscription.
Debt fund analysis is much weaker than equity fund analysis. Credit quality breakdown, YTM, maturity profile — some of these are missing or not clearly displayed. Debt investors are underserved here.
The exit load and lock-in period information is clearly displayed on every fund page. This is important for planning redemptions and I'm glad it's visible without needing Pro.
The direct vs regular plan comparison is useful for understanding how much I'm losing to distributor commissions. The cost difference visualization over 10-20 years is eye-opening.
Category-level comparison is limited. I want to see the top 10 funds in ELSS sorted by 5-year alpha with expense ratio overlay. The current filtering is functional but not as granular as I'd like.
I love the goal-based tracking feature. I've mapped each SIP to a life goal — retirement, child education, house down payment — and the projected corpus calculator keeps me motivated.

The CAMS import for mutual fund portfolios doesn't work half the time. I spent 30 minutes trying to import my 8-year SIP history and it kept timing out. This is the most critical feature for MF investors and it needs to be robust.
I track NFOs here and the new fund offer section with AMC details, fund manager background, and category benchmarking helps me decide whether an NFO is worth investing in. Very practical tool.
International fund analysis is weak. I invest in global funds and the underlying holdings, geographical exposure, and currency risk sections are either absent or very shallow for international MFs.
The ability to filter mutual funds by sectoral allocation is very handy. I wanted exposure to manufacturing-themed funds and could quickly find all funds with high manufacturing sector weights.

The mutual fund page is well-organized but I wish there was a one-tap 'Start SIP' button that took me directly to my preferred platform. Right now, I have to leave Tickertape and open Coin or Groww separately.

The XIRR vs category average comparison tells me whether my fund selection is actually beating passive alternatives. This is a sophisticated metric that most apps don't show. Very glad Tickertape has it.

The free MF screener is so limited that it's basically unusable for serious MF research. You can filter by category and returns, and that's about it. Every meaningful metric like Sortino ratio or max drawdown is Pro-only.
A few of my SIPs don't show up in the portfolio section despite being linked from CAMS. This missing data throws off my overall portfolio analysis. It's been a persistent bug for 3 months.
The expert opinion section on each MF — curated views from registered advisors — is very helpful for someone who doesn't want to go deep into the numbers. Helps me sanity-check my picks.

Tax efficiency analysis for mutual funds — showing LTCG, STCG implications based on holding period — is a feature I haven't seen well-implemented elsewhere. Tickertape's tax overlay on returns is genuinely useful.

I came to Tickertape specifically for MF research and found that most useful filters are behind Pro. Screener.in gives more free MF data. For casual MF investors, the free tier is just not good enough.
The Consistent Performers screen for mutual funds — filtering funds with above-benchmark performance across multiple time periods — is a great shortcut for finding reliable long-term performers.

The multi-broker portfolio sync is the main reason I use Tickertape. I have accounts with Zerodha, Upstox, and HDFC Securities. Seeing all of them in one consolidated view with sector-level breakdowns is excellent.
My Motilal Oswal account doesn't sync with Tickertape. It's been listed as a supported broker for months but every time I try to link it, I get an authentication error. Support has been unhelpful.

The diversification score methodology is well-explained. I can see my portfolio broken down by market cap, sector, theme, and asset class. It's helped me identify that I'm too concentrated in mid-caps.
Portfolio sync is not real-time. Holdings update only once a day. If I buy a stock in the morning, it doesn't reflect in my Tickertape portfolio until the next day. This needs to be more frequent.

The red flags feature is genuinely impressive. It proactively flagged that one of my holdings had declining promoter holding, rising pledging, and poor audit observations. That combination of warnings was very timely.
The Zerodha integration works well but after every Kite update, the linkage breaks and I have to re-authenticate. This is annoying. The integration should be more resilient to broker app updates.
The realized P&L and unrealized P&L breakdown is useful for tax planning. Seeing how much STCG vs LTCG I've accumulated before March helps me decide whether to book losses before year-end.

The Upstox sync was completely broken for two weeks. I filed a support ticket and got a response after 7 days saying they were working on it. In the meantime, my portfolio analysis was entirely off. Very poor for a pro subscriber.

The peer comparison within my own portfolio is clever. I can see how my individual stock picks are performing vs their sector index. Helps me identify which bets have been right and which have lagged.
Manual addition of holdings not linked via brokers is a bit clunky. Adding pre-IPO shares, unlisted stocks, or RSUs manually requires too many steps. A simpler manual entry flow would help.
The portfolio overlap analysis between my stocks and the mutual funds I hold is a killer feature. Found that my direct equity bets had 70% overlap with my flexi-cap fund, making the fund redundant.
Portfolio analysis beyond basic P&L is entirely locked behind Pro. Even the sector allocation pie chart is paywalled on the free tier. Without this, the portfolio tracker is just a basic P&L viewer.

The 'compare with Nifty 500' benchmark comparison for my portfolio CAGR is very useful. It gives me an honest answer to whether my stock picking is adding value or if I'd be better off in an index fund.
ICICI Direct integration works but it only pulls equity holdings. My ICICI FDs and bonds are not reflected. A truly consolidated net worth view needs to include all asset types.
The corporate actions alert — informing me when a stock in my portfolio announces dividend, bonus, or buyback — is a very useful feature. Saves me from missing important events.

The portfolio performance calculation is wrong for stocks where I've done partial sell-offs. The XIRR gets incorrectly computed when there are multiple buy and sell transactions. This is a serious calculation bug.

I track 4 family members' portfolios on one account using different watchlists mapped to each person. While this is a workaround, the multi-watchlist feature is flexible enough to support this use case.

The risk assessment feature is useful in concept but the methodology isn't transparent. I don't know how Tickertape defines 'high risk' for a stock. A scoring methodology document would build confidence.

Getting a single-screen view of my equity, MF, gold, and FD holdings is very convenient. The net worth widget on the home screen showing total invested value with day's change is clean and satisfying.

Not all brokers are equally well-supported. My Kotak Securities account takes almost 24 hours to sync while my Zerodha syncs within hours. The consistency of sync speed across brokers needs improvement.
The ability to tag my investments by goal — retirement, house, car — and track goal-wise progress is a feature I didn't know I needed until I used it. Now it's central to my financial planning.

After a recent Tickertape update, my Groww portfolio sync stopped working. The holdings showed as zero. Took 3 days of back-and-forth with support to fix. Such regressions should not happen on a paid product.
The tax harvesting suggestions — identifying which holdings are currently at a short-term loss that I could book to offset STCG — is a very practical feature for tax-savvy investors.

The portfolio page takes 15-20 seconds to fully load with 30+ stocks and mutual funds. Compared to the Kite app which loads near-instantly, this is noticeably slow. Caching and lazy loading need to be implemented.
I appreciate the downloadable portfolio report as a PDF. I use it for my annual financial review and share it with my financial advisor. Clean formatting and comprehensive data.

The US stocks feature is new and shows promise. 7,000+ stocks is a good starting universe. But the research depth for US companies is significantly thinner than what I get for Indian stocks. Basic financials only.

Tried to fund my US investing account and the remittance process took 5 business days. The app said 2-3 days. When markets are moving, a 5-day fund transfer is way too slow. Need to fix remittance speed.

Fractional shares with just $1 is an excellent entry point for Indian investors who want global diversification without committing large amounts. The concept and UX around fractional investing is well thought out.

The US stock screener is much weaker than the Indian stock screener. Only about 20-30 filters vs 200+ for Indian stocks. For US-focused research, I still rely on Finviz. Please build out the US screener.

I tried to withdraw funds from my US investing account. It's been 6 days and the money hasn't arrived. Customer support replied once saying they're investigating and then went silent. Completely unacceptable.
The GIFT City route for US investing gives me legal and tax compliance without the headache of LRS paperwork that other apps require. The KYC was fully digital and took 8 minutes. Very smooth.
ETF selection for US markets is decent but not great. Only about 200-300 ETFs vs the 2,500+ available on US exchanges. Missing some key thematic ETFs I wanted. Hope they expand the universe.

Investing in Apple, Google, and Nvidia from India in rupees with a familiar interface is something I've wanted for years. Tickertape makes it genuinely easy. The currency conversion is transparent and the costs are fair.

The US portfolio P&L doesn't correctly account for currency fluctuation in a transparent way. My return is showing differently when I calculate manually. Need a clearer breakdown of stock returns vs INR/USD exchange impact.
The US stock research pages don't show options data, short interest, or insider trading activity. For US stocks these are commonly tracked metrics and their absence limits my research capability.
The ability to set price alerts on US stocks in INR terms is very useful. I don't have to constantly convert USD prices in my head. This India-specific UX thinking is appreciated.

Tax reporting for US investments — FEMA compliance, reporting requirements — is unclear within the app. I'd love an in-app guide to the tax implications of US investing through GIFT City so I know what to declare.
The discovery section highlighting US ETFs by theme — AI, clean energy, semiconductors — is helpful for Indian investors who don't know where to start with US markets. Good curation.

Order execution for US stocks during US market hours means I have to set orders at odd Indian timings. There's no pre-market order scheduling. I want to set limit orders that execute during the US session automatically.

The US portfolio and Indian portfolio are separate views with separate analytics. I want a single consolidated portfolio view that shows my total equity exposure across Indian and US markets together.
I appreciate that the app shows the Nifty 50 vs S&P 500 correlation analysis. Understanding how my global diversification reduces portfolio risk in real numbers is educational and motivating.

Had a transaction discrepancy in my US investing account — a buy order was executed but the stock never appeared in my portfolio. Raised a ticket and got one automated response. Still unresolved after 8 days. This is a money issue and needs priority support.

The US stock screener doesn't include revenue growth or profit margin filters. These are basic fundamental filters that any investor would want. The Indian screener is far more advanced. US should be brought to parity.
The 'Brands You Use Every Day' framing for US stocks is a great way to help Indian investors connect with US companies they know. It lowers the psychological barrier to global investing.

Market hours and timezone confusion is a minor but real friction. The app doesn't clearly indicate whether a US stock price I'm seeing is real-time, delayed, or from the last US session close. A clear data-freshness indicator is needed.

Tickertape has become my annual review tool. I export my entire portfolio performance, check my XIRR vs Nifty 50, review my diversification score, and recalibrate allocations. It handles this structured review process beautifully.

The goal-based investing tracker is a good concept but needs a retirement corpus calculator that accounts for inflation-adjusted withdrawal. Currently the goal tracker only shows corpus accumulation, not the distribution phase.
Being a passive investor, the index fund filtering on the MF screener is useful. I can compare tracking error, expense ratio, and AUM growth for Nifty 50 index funds across AMCs to pick the best one.
The asset allocation tracker doesn't include real estate or EPF/PPF. For someone targeting financial independence, these form a large part of net worth. Tickertape only tracks financial assets.
The long-term SIP performance simulation showing what monthly investments of various amounts grow to over 20-30 years — accounting for historical category returns — is my favorite planning feature.

The comparison between my actual portfolio CAGR and a benchmark passive portfolio is very honest feedback. It showed me clearly that my mid-cap active bets have underperformed a simple index fund over 5 years.

For long-term investors, having accurate corporate action history — every bonus, split, rights issue — is critical for correct CAGR calculations. Found 2 stocks where the corporate action data was missing, leading to wrong return figures.

The dividend income tracker is excellent for dividend growth investors. I can see my annual dividend income trend year over year. A projected dividend income based on current yield would make this feature even more powerful.

The annual Pro subscription at ₹2,399 is fair value. But it should include multi-user access for family portfolios. I manage investments for myself, my spouse, and parents — four separate subscriptions is expensive.
Tickertape helped me consolidate my SIP research onto one platform and simplify my portfolio from 12 funds to 4. The overlap analysis and consistency metrics were key to making those decisions.
The shareholding pattern data sourced from quarterly filings is accurate and current. I rely on this to track management's skin in the game and institutional ownership trends.
When I open the app, the first thing I see is advertisements for smallcases and fixed deposits. I just want to see the market overview. The home screen feels too commercial.
The app is slower than Kite or Upstox Pro. For research before or during trades, every second counts. The page load time and chart rendering needs to be much faster.
The comparison of a lump sum vs SIP investment outcome for any fund is a feature I use regularly to decide how to deploy money. Clear, intuitive, and very practical.
The broker link authentication expires randomly and I have to re-link periodically. An auto-renewal or background refresh without manual re-authentication would significantly improve the experience.

I built a 'Quality at a Reasonable Price' screener combining high ROE, low debt, consistent earnings growth, and reasonable PE. Finding 15 quality stocks to deep-dive is now a 15-minute exercise instead of hours.
The price alert setup is very easy — just long press on a stock and set the target. Simple and intuitive. Got my first alert notification within minutes of the stock hitting my price. Great feature.
The portfolio page with many MF holdings loads slowly, especially on 4G. Need better optimization and offline-first caching for previously loaded portfolio data.
The real-time US market indices — S&P 500, Nasdaq, Dow — on the home page give me a quick pulse check before the Indian markets open. Good contextual addition.

The screener is great for identifying candidates but I can't annotate or add personal notes to screener results. If I could tag stocks with my own comments like 'watch for Q3 results' it would be a much better research workflow.
Annual portfolio review in January is something I now do entirely on Tickertape. The data export, P&L summary, and sector allocation breakdown give me everything I need for a systematic review.
The in-app support only links to an FAQ page. There is no chat or phone option. For a first-time investor confused about a feature, this is very unhelpful. Need to add at least a live chat option.
The sectoral concentration alert — notifying when a single sector crosses 40% of portfolio — is a helpful guardrail for investors who tend to chase hot sectors.

International revenue exposure data for Indian companies is missing. For a company like Infosys or Sun Pharma where >50% revenue is international, this geographic breakdown should be visible. Important for currency risk assessment.
The mutual fund category education section explaining what large-cap, flexi-cap, and hybrid funds are — with examples — is excellent content for people new to MF investing.
Stock screener result alerts — notifying me when a stock enters or exits my custom screen — would be a game-changing feature. Currently I have to manually re-run screens to see new entries.
The market indices dashboard with NIFTY, NIFTY Bank, SENSEX, and sector indices in one scrollable view is very convenient. Clean presentation of what's happening in the market at a glance.
I wish the portfolio could track physical gold and PPF contributions alongside financial assets. For a complete net worth picture, these fixed-income and commodity holdings matter.
The news feed for US stocks is decent but skewed toward mainstream tech names. For less-covered US stocks, the news section is often empty. Integration with Seeking Alpha or Benzinga would help.
The management quality screening proxies — low capital misallocation, consistent dividend growth, no related-party transactions flagged — are thoughtful additions for fundamentals-focused investors.

Would appreciate a family plan pricing tier. Managing financial portfolios for multiple family members on separate Pro accounts is unnecessarily expensive. Even a 2-user plan at 1.5x would be worth it.

The onboarding asks me about my investment goals upfront but then doesn't use those answers to personalize the experience. If I said I'm a beginner interested in MFs, the app should highlight MF features more prominently.
The derivative statistics section — OI data, PCR, put/call spreads — is a useful addition for traders who use F&O as market signals even if they don't directly trade derivatives.

Every single time I update the Tickertape app, my broker link breaks and I need to re-authenticate all three accounts. This regression-per-update pattern is exhausting and needs to be fixed architecturally.

I used Tickertape's 10-year category-average return data to build my asset allocation strategy. The historical return and drawdown data per mutual fund category was the single most useful reference I found anywhere.
The option to download 10 years of quarterly financials in a structured Excel format would be very useful for building DCF models. Right now the export only covers annual data and limited periods.
Tickertape is the only finance app I've recommended to my non-finance friends. The language is simple, the visuals are clear, and it doesn't make you feel stupid for not knowing financial jargon.
The currency risk warning when I invest in US stocks is a legal disclaimer, not an actual analytical tool. I'd love to see historical INR/USD returns incorporated into US stock return analysis.
The staggered SIP tracking showing each tranche, its NAV at purchase, current NAV, and individual tranche return is beautifully detailed. Helps me understand which months I got good entry prices.
A sectoral MMI would be very useful. The overall market sentiment can be in Greed while specific sectors are in Fear. That divergence is exactly where trading opportunities lie.
The fund comparison feature allowing side-by-side metric comparison of 2 mutual funds is well-designed. The returns across rolling periods side-by-side makes the choice immediately clear.
I use the low-churn, low-volatility screener to find stocks suitable for a long-term buy-and-hold FIRE portfolio. The combination of business stability metrics available in the screener is excellent.

The 60+ custom filter promise in Pro is slightly misleading. Some 'advanced' filters are actually just basic ratios with a different name. The marginal value of going from free to Pro is less than the marketing suggests.
